name: Jessie Ware
label: EMI / Interscope
lede: Jessie Ware went from newsroom desks and backing vocals to a Mercury shortlisting, nearly quit after her third album, then built a second act out of a podcast with her mum and a disco record.

eras.title: Singing from the side of the stage
eras.text: Before any solo record, Jessie Ware was a journalist, a TV researcher and a touring backing singer. Two introductions from the dance world, SBTRKT and Sampha, turned her into the voice people in London were asking about.

years.cap: Jessie Ware with Jack Peñate, January 2010
years.h: Ware writes for the Jewish Chronicle and sings for Jack Peñate
years.p: After Sussex she worked at the Jewish Chronicle, on the Daily Mirror's sports desk and at the TV company Love Productions, and toured as a backing vocalist for [[Jack Peñate|9b64cf5d-1f4a-45b5-a84a-5109a88f178f]], including in the US.
years.xp:
Ware grew up in Clapham and went to Alleyn's School in Dulwich, where Florence Welch, Peñate and Felix White of the Maccabees were schoolmates. She studied English literature at the University of Sussex.

Peñate's tour is where she learned to be a front person from the side of the stage. She has credited it as training for her solo career.

years.h: SBTRKT puts her on "Nervous"
years.p: Peñate's bandmate Tic made the introduction. Ware's vocal on SBTRKT's "Nervous", out on PMR, was the first record with her voice on it that got noticed.
years.xp: The PMR connection led to "The Vision", a collaboration with the DJ Joker, which Wikipedia says helped seal her own deal with the label.

years.h: "Valentine" comes out on a heart-shaped record
years.p: Ware met [[Sampha|130c2184-14f2-4180-a216-04b5a333be57]] through SBTRKT, and Young Turks pressed their duet on heart-shaped vinyl.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the song was partly inspired by a James Blake track and by the couple's own romantic experiences. Ware also sang on Florence and the Machine's 2011 album Ceremonials, for a school friend.

years.h: A purple 10-inch that missed the chart
years.p: "Strangest Feeling", her first solo single, came out through PMR on limited purple vinyl and didn't register on the UK Singles Chart.

eras.title: A Mercury nod and a rapper's verse
eras.text: Devotion made her a name in the UK, put her on the Mercury shortlist and crossed to the US with an A$AP Rocky verse attached. She spent 2013 touring it.

years.h: "Running" arrives six months ahead of the album
years.p: The lead single from Devotion came out on her PMR and Island deal. Wikipedia lists it at No. 41 in the UK.
years.xp:
Dave Okumu and Julio Bashmore produced it. Wikipedia describes a yacht-rock groove, and reviewers compared Ware's vocal to Sade's.

A Disclosure remix followed on April 4, 2012.

years.h: Devotion lands at No. 5 with Dave Okumu behind most of it
years.p: Okumu, of the Invisible, produced twelve of the fourteen original tracks. It went on to UK Gold.
years.xp:
The first week sold 9,319 copies. The Guardian wrote that for all the album's poise and restraint, dance music "clearly runs through" the vocalist's veins; the Metacritic score is 85 from 28 reviews. Pitchfork later put it on its list of the 100 best albums of 2010 to 2014.

One song changed names: "110%" was first titled "If You're Never Gonna Move" after sample clearance disputes over a Big Pun interpolation.

years.cap: Jessie Ware, January 2012, before Devotion came out
years.h: Devotion makes the Mercury shortlist
years.p: The album sat on the shortlist for Album of the Year, with MOBO and Brit nominations for best female and breakthrough act around it.
years.xp:
It did not win the Mercury. The Brit nominations came at the 2013 ceremony, in the female and breakthrough categories.

Pitchfork gave the album 8.5.

years.h: A$AP Rocky adds a verse for the US release
years.p: Devotion reached the States on April 16 via Cherrytree and Interscope, with a Gold Edition of four extra tracks and a "Wildest Moments" remix.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Ware was promoting in the States and Rocky's verses arrived just before the deadline. The US edition left off "Valentine", her duet with Sampha. The Billboard 200 peak was No. 79.

Cherrytree had signed the US distribution deal the previous October.

eras.title: Bigger rooms, a baby, an album to redo
eras.text: Tough Love went bigger and more pop, and gave her her best-known single. Then came a break from performing, a baby in 2016 and a third album she wasn't happy with.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tough Love (Jessie Ware album) · Wikipedia: Jessie Ware
years.h: Tough Love goes to No. 9 with Dev Hynes, Miguel and BenZel in the credits
years.p: Her second album went Gold in the UK, and the title track gave her a first UK top-40 single, at No. 34.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Ware's own page disagree on the UK release date: October 6 and October 13. Metacritic has it at 74 from 26 reviews. Pitchfork wrote that "rarely does a major-label pop singer sound as tasteful as Ware does."

Ware also sang the chorus on "The Crying Game" for Nicki Minaj's 2014 album The Pinkprint.

years.big: "With Ed in Benny's tiny bedroom studio in New York."
q: With Ed in Benny's tiny bedroom studio in New York.
years.src: Double J: Ten years in, Jessie Ware is enjoying her career more than ever · Wikipedia: Tough Love (Jessie Ware album)
years.h: "Say You Love Me" becomes her biggest UK hit
years.p: Ware co-wrote it with [[Ed Sheeran|b8a7c51f-362c-4dcb-a259-bc6e0095f0a6]] and [[Benny Blanco|5a6131f9-f8db-4722-b4d7-6a0c7183c590]], and it peaked at No. 22. She told Double J it was one of her proudest moments.
years.xp: Ware later co-wrote "New Man" on Sheeran's 2017 album ÷ and sang backing vocals on it.

years.h: A live "Wildest Moments" from the Roundhouse
years.p: The iTunes Festival in London filmed her set during the Tough Love year.

years.h: Benny Blanco hears the third album and tells her to start over
years.p: His verdict in December 2016, on a rushed first pass at Glasshouse, per Wikipedia's account.
years.xp:
Ware had rushed to finish the record before her baby arrived in September 2016 and wasn't satisfied. Blanco asked why she wasn't making the music she actually wanted to.

She rebuilt the album with new sessions, including with Starsmith and James Newman, and named Childish Gambino's Awaken, My Love!, Solange's A Seat at the Table and Christine and the Queens as reference points.

eras.title: Close to quitting, with a podcast on the side
eras.text: Glasshouse landed softly and Ware seriously considered ending her music career. A podcast with her mother gave her a different job, and a new label and management gave her a different record.

years.h: Glasshouse opens at No. 7, her third straight top-ten debut
years.p: It sold 8,448 units in week one and got mixed-to-good reviews. The title comes from an Edward Thomas poem.
years.xp:
Metacritic averaged 72 from 13 reviews. AllMusic noted "finely woven adult-pop ballads" but a "stitched-together quality"; Clash found it too safe. The cover is Ware at Neuendorf House in Mallorca, a 1991 modernist villa by John Pawson and Claudio Silvestrin.

Collaborators included Benny Blanco, Ed Sheeran, Julia Michaels, Cashmere Cat, Kid Harpoon and Francis and the Lights.

years.cap: Jessie Ware live, November 5, 2017, on the Glasshouse tour
years.src: Table Manners: About · Wikipedia: Jessie Ware
years.h: Sam Smith is the first guest at the Wares' table
years.p: Jessie and her mother Lennie Ware launch Table Manners for Acast and Island Records, a podcast where famous people eat dinner with them.
years.xp:
The show has run for 18 series and more than 200 episodes, and its own site claims over 60 million downloads. It won Best New Voice at the 2018 Audio Production Awards and Best Podcast at the 2022 NME Awards.

Guests have included Ed Sheeran, Nigella Lawson, Daniel Kaluuya, Paul McCartney and Kylie Minogue. A cookbook followed in 2020.

years.cap: Jessie Ware at the Jazz Cafe, London, February 22, 2018
years.big: "I'd had a child and was trying to show everybody I could be everything."
q: I'd had a child and was trying to show everybody I could be everything.
years.src: Double J: Ten years in, Jessie Ware is enjoying her career more than ever · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware · Wikipedia: What's Your Pleasure?
years.h: Ware starts to think the career might be over
years.p: Glasshouse left her feeling it would all finish, she told Double J, and she considered leaving music.
years.xp: She has said the podcast made her more comfortable in her skin and let her talk about her life without pressure to put it all into songs. Music Week's 2023 profile names her new management, Fascination (Peter Loraine and Sarah Jackson), and Universal UK chairman David Joseph as people who pushed her toward a change of label.

years.h: The disco starts with "Adore You"
years.p: The February 2019 single was the first of the run that became What's Your Pleasure?.

eras.title: Lockdown disco
eras.text: A record made with James Ford, pitched as a party she couldn't throw during a pandemic. It became her first UK top-three album and the turn the rest of her story runs on.

years.src: Wikipedia: What's Your Pleasure? · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware
years.h: What's Your Pleasure? goes to No. 3 in lockdown
years.p: Delayed twice, it became her first UK top-three entry; Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
The first date was June 5, then June 19, then June 26, pushed back by COVID and by Juneteenth. Ford co-produced and co-wrote; Metacritic has it at 84 from 18 reviews. Ware described it as a two-year labour of love about escapism.

Music Week's profile puts its sales at 66,426, below Devotion's 140,486, though it peaked higher on the chart.

years.h: A Platinum Pleasure Edition adds seven songs
years.p: The reissue added "Overtime", "Please", "Hot N Heavy" and an "Adore You" remix, in grayscale metallic packaging.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kiss of Life (Kylie Minogue and Jessie Ware song)
years.h: Ware says she bullied Kylie Minogue into a duet
years.p: The joke followed Minogue's September 2020 Table Manners appearance; James Ford produced "Kiss of Life".
years.xp: The song is on the reissue Disco: Guest List Edition; Minogue sang her part remotely from Melbourne. Sophie Muller shot the video at London's Ave Mario restaurant, inspired by Pedro Almodovar and 1980s telenovelas, with Ware as restaurateur and Minogue as food critic.

eras.title: A Park stage and a prize list
eras.text: The disco record's sequel was louder, funnier and built for crowds. A Glastonbury headline slot opened it, and Pitchfork, the Guardian and the Mercury list all noticed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Free Yourself (Jessie Ware song) · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware
yt: "Spotlight" and "Save A Kiss", Best Kept Secret 2022
years.h: "Free Yourself" gets its first play on the Park stage
years.p: Ware played the new song in her Glastonbury Park stage headline set. The single followed on July 19.
years.xp: Stuart Price produced; Ware, Price and Clarence Coffee Jr. wrote it. Pitchfork put it at No. 49 on its year-end songs list, and Billboard at No. 33. Music Week's 2023 profile says she had supported Harry Styles and headlined the Park stage.

years.h: A ruby red dress, a stately home and a touch of the occult
years.p: Vicky Lawton directed the "Free Yourself" video and called it "very '70s rock 'n' roll".

years.cap: Jessie Ware at Alexandra Palace, London, November 17, 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: That! Feels Good! · Album of the Year: Jessie Ware, That! Feels Good! reviews · Under the Radar: Jessie Ware, That! Feels Good! review
years.h: Pitchfork puts That! Feels Good! at No. 22 for 2023
years.p: Her fifth album reached No. 3 in the UK, and Julianne Escobedo Shepherd's Pitchfork review scored it 8.3.
years.xp:
Julianne Escobedo Shepherd wrote the Pitchfork review; per Wikipedia it calls the album "a genre revival album that's painstakingly true to its source material, but doesn't sound like a curdled rehash." Metacritic has 89; NME, the Guardian and the Financial Times gave five stars.

In the US it reached No. 16 on Top Album Sales, her highest since Tough Love. Stuart Price and James Ford produced, and Ware co-wrote with Shungudzo, Danny Parker, Clarence Coffee Jr. and Sarah Hudson. The title track opens with spoken cameos from Kylie Minogue, Gemma Arterton and Roisin Murphy. Rolling Stone put it at No. 18 and NME at No. 20 on year-end lists; PopMatters ranked it No. 1 of pop albums.

years.h: Roisin Murphy sings "Freak Me Now" from an airport toilet
years.p: The fourth single from That! Feels Good! features [[Roisin Murphy|4c56405d-ba8e-4283-99c3-1dc95bdd50e7]], who also has a spoken cameo on the title track.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Murphy recorded her vocals in an airport toilet. The song came out July 27, 2023 and leans on French house.

years.h: A second Mercury shortlisting, eleven years after the first
years.p: That! Feels Good! was Ware's first nomination since Devotion in 2012. Ezra Collective won, announced September 7, 2023.

eras.title: Superbloom, then the arenas
eras.text: A sixth album that keeps the dance floor but reaches for more grown-up intimacy, with her first arena tour ahead.

years.cap: Jessie Ware on the Superbloom run, April 20, 2026
years.h: Superbloom debuts at No. 2, her highest peak yet
years.p: The EMI album has production from Ford and Price, plus Xenomania's Miranda Cooper and Jon Shave on the lead single.
years.xp:
Reviews were generally favorable: Metacritic 76. The Guardian felt it failed to deliver the jolt of What's Your Pleasure?, and Paste found it less fresh. Ware acts as her own A&R, as she has since 2020.

The Superbloom Tour, her first arena run, starts October 6, 2026 in Toronto and finishes December 5 in Manchester.
